voyage.content: The city's main concert hall, capacity 2200, and home to the Royal Scottish National Orchestra. It was completed in 1914, funded by Andrew Usher the whisky distiller and blender.

voyage.name: Royal Lyceum
voyage.content: Completed in 1883 and little altered since, this is home to the Royal Lyceum Theatre Company.

voyage.name: Traverse Theatre
voyage.content: Since 1992 this has hosted Traverse theatre company, dedicated to new works.

voyage.name: King's Theatre
voyage.content: Reopened in August 2026 after 4 years of refurbishment.

voyage.name: Cameo Cinema
voyage.content: Mainstream, arthouse and alternative films, with an Edwardian interior.

voyage.name: Odeon Cinema
voyage.content: Mostly mainstream movies.

voyage.name: Red Door Gallery
voyage.content: Arts and crafts and giftware.

voyage.name: Armstrongs
voyage.content: A local institution, this has a huge stock of vintage clothing and uniforms, including pre-hirpled kilts.

voyage.name: Underground Solu'shn
voyage.content: A great little record store dealing mainly in dance/electro music.

voyage.name: Cadenhead's Whisky Shop
voyage.content: This Campbeltown-based firm is an independent bottler of whisky and other spirits (a rarity nowadays), so they do bespoke sales and samplers.

voyage.name: Focus
voyage.content: Skatewear and skateboard store, friendly knowledgeable staff.

voyage.name: The Piemaker
voyage.content: This has a wide range of delicious pies and savoury pastries, piping hot. They're mostly a takeaway and don't deliver, but have a few seats inside.

voyage.name: Kebab Mahal
voyage.content: Good halal curries, kebabs and tandooris, no alcohol.

voyage.name: The Original Mosque Kitchen
voyage.content: Inexpensive chicken or vegetable curry. A favorite with generations of Edinburgh University students for its cost and portion sizes.

voyage.name: Tempting Tattie
voyage.content: Inexpensive takeaway for trad baked potatoes.

voyage.name: Kampong Ah Lee
voyage.content: Tasty Malaysian dishes such as Roti Canai, Satay, Nasi Lemak, Laksa and Rendang.

voyage.name: Em’s Kitchen
voyage.content: Full Scottish breakfast, shakshuka, coffee and tea options, with seating that looks into a quiet car park and garden.

voyage.name: John's Coffee House & Tavern
voyage.content: Located in a historic building. Breakfast, all-day waffles, light lunch options, small plates to share, bar with wide range of Scotch whiskies.

voyage.name: The Everest
voyage.content: Good inexpensive Nepalese and Indian food.

voyage.name: Petit Paris
voyage.content: Traditional French restaurant complete with chequered tablecloths and whitewashed walls.

voyage.name: David Bann
voyage.content: Imaginative and tasty vegetarian food, with lots available for vegans or GF.

voyage.name: Whiski
voyage.content: A bit touristy, but a good choice for Scottish food, drink and music. Hundreds of whiskies available, bar staff happy to advise. Live music every night from 9:30PM, try to sit up front for this.

voyage.name: Nok's Kitchen
voyage.content: Decent Thai food with vegetarian options. They add 10% service to the menu prices.

voyage.name: Kanpai Sushi
voyage.content: Small portions of sushi and other Japanese food, and pricey, but speedy service and memorable quality.

voyage.name: Gurkha
voyage.content: Traditional Indian and Nepalese restaurant.

voyage.name: Kalpana
voyage.content: Long-established quality vegetarian Indian restaurant serving curries, thalis and tandooris.

voyage.name: Tanjore
voyage.content: One of the few places in Edinburgh serving South Indian food such as Dosas, Uttapams, Sambar and other Tamil specialities.

voyage.name: MUMS
voyage.content: Classic British comfort food: haggis, fish & chips, sausage & mash, stews, or shepherd's pie. Lots of veggie choices, no reservations.

voyage.name: The Elephant House
voyage.content: Consistently good coffee and light bites, cafe is full of university and creative types; JK Rowling wrote much of the first Harry Potter book here. And that alas is the problem: it's become part of the Potter circus, every half hour sees another coachload of tourists all craning for selfies and trying to nick the cutlery and scrawling graffiti in the loo. Prices, service and ambience have suffered accordingly, and Ro

voyage.name: The Witchery by the Castle
voyage.content: By the castle entrance, The Witchery serves top-class food in an elegant candle-lit restaurant. They've now added rooms, flamboyantly camp.

voyage.name: Timberyard
voyage.content: Outstanding Scottish cuisine in a 19th century warehouse, with extensive wine list. One Michelin star, the head chef is Jimmy Murray.

voyage.name: The Jolly Judge
voyage.hours: Tue Wed noon-11PM, Thu-Sat, Mon noon-midnight, Sun 2PM-11PM
voyage.content: Cosy independent pub with a good selection of beer and whisky. One of the few pubs on Royal Mile that's not a tourist trap.

voyage.name: Albanach
voyage.content: Cosy Belhaven pub with food and whisky.

voyage.name: Doctors
voyage.content: Now a Belhaven pub, this is a welcoming place with good ales and food. It was a few yards from the former Royal Infirmary, within bleep range and sprinting distance for the junior doctors.

voyage.name: Sandy Bells
voyage.content: Likewise frequented by medical students, this has live folk music every night.

voyage.name: The Pear Tree
voyage.content: Popular with students, this has a large beer garden and outdoor big screen for TV sports.

voyage.name: The Kilderkin
voyage.content: Fair selection of cask ales and whisky, the food is so-so and the warmth of welcome varies. This is the original of a chain that now includes The Windsor on Elm Row, Blue Blazer on Spittal St and Bennets at Tolcross.

voyage.name: The Bow Bar
voyage.content: Old-style boozer with a large selection of whiskies, selection of guest ales, and no background music.

voyage.name: Bennets Bar
voyage.content: A good old-fashioned pub, now part of Kilderkin group, with a wide selection of real ale and whisky. It is traditionally the place for pre / post-theatre drinks, with the Kings Theatre.

voyage.name: The Bongo Club
voyage.content: A café-bar and live music venue.

voyage.name: Cabaret Voltaire
voyage.content: Atmospheric basement vault with regular gigs.

voyage.name: Dragonfly
voyage.content: Well-hidden but popular cocktail lounge.

voyage.name: The Jazz Bar
voyage.content: Live music every night, majoring on jazz; early shows are generally free, later gigs individually priced. Limited food or seating.

voyage.name: The Liquid Room
voyage.content: 800-capacity live music venue.

voyage.name: Wash Bar
voyage.content: Modern pub, mostly a local crowd, TV sport, no food.

voyage.name: 56 North
voyage.content: Cocktail bar incorporating South Loch gin distillery.

voyage.name: Motel One Edinburgh Royal
voyage.content: Comfy efficient place by the station, great value. They have another branch by the bus station.

voyage.name: Kick Ass Greyfriars
voyage.content: Cheerful friendly staff and modern amenities. Offers dormitory beds and 2-4 bed private rooms.

voyage.name: Code The Court
voyage.content: Hybrid hostel/hotel in a former jail and courtroom. Offers pod capsules and private rooms.

voyage.name: Castle Rock Hostel
voyage.content: Clean spacious hostel with 300 beds on the hill just below Castle Esplanade.

voyage.name: ibis Edinburgh Centre South Bridge
voyage.content: Reliable chain hotel.

voyage.name: ibis Edinburgh Centre Royal Mile - Hunter Square
voyage.content: Slick welcoming inexpensive hotel.

voyage.name: Premier Inn Edinburgh City Centre
voyage.content: Good reliable chain hotel by the station.

voyage.name: Leonardo Royal Hotel
voyage.content: Good value place next to the railway station.

voyage.name: Ten Hill Place Hotel
voyage.content: Central but quiet hotel in a Georgian terrace with 78 bedrooms.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Express
voyage.content: They call it "Royal Mile" but it's in the dark canyon of Cowgate 200 yards south - still a very central location, and value for money.

voyage.name: Edinburgh Holyrood Hotel
voyage.content: Now part of Marriott chain, this is under renovation but remains open.

voyage.name: Apex Grassmarket
voyage.content: Comfy place to stay with great views of the castle.

voyage.name: Apex City of Edinburgh
voyage.content: Similar price and quality to their branch at No 31.

voyage.name: Hotel du Vin
voyage.content: Great comfort, service and location beyond its price bracket.

voyage.name: Novotel
voyage.content: Mid-range chain near Tolcross.

voyage.name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Edinburgh City Centre
voyage.content: Comfy hotel near Usher Hall, short walk to the castle.

voyage.name: The Scotsman
voyage.content: This iconic building stands like a castle guarding the entrance to Old Town from North Bridge. From 1904 to 2001 it housed The Scotsman newspaper, with editors and reporters above, printing presses below, and newspapers loaded onto trains from the basement. After they moved out it became an upscale hotel, charmingly refurbished within and scoring highly for comfort, service and location.

voyage.name: Hilton Edinburgh Carlton
voyage.content: Great location, service and comfort mostly good, some construction noise.

voyage.name: Sheraton Grand Hotel
voyage.content: Part of Marriott chain, great location and for most visitors great comfort, but housekeeping is too erratic for what you pay.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel
voyage.content: Great location, comfort and service. The hotel was built in 1990, but with a retro-antique facade to blend with neighbouring buildings.

voyage.name: Cheval Old Town Chambers
voyage.content: This knock-through of medieval tenements was designed as luxury serviced apartments, but has added common areas to create a townhouse hotel.

voyage.name: Radisson Collection Hotel
voyage.content: Closed for refurbishment.
